\begin{theorem}[A large singleton Fourier coefficient]
\lean{FABL.exists_singletonCoeff_ge_edgeKKL}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p276-b008}
\label{FABL.exists_singletonCoeff_ge_edgeKKL}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.IsNonconstantProductFunction, FABL.PMFHasFullSupport, FABL.Sign, FABL.booleanInfluence_eq_influence_toReal, FABL.dimension_pos_of_nonconstant, FABL.edgeKKL, FABL.exists_booleanInfluence_eq_maximumInfluence, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.influence_eq_fourierCoeff_singleton_of_monotone, FABL.productVariance, FABL.productVariance_pos_of_nonconstant, FABL.productVariance_uniformSign, FABL.signValue_injective, FABL.totalInfluence, FABL.uniformPMF, FABL.variance}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ be a monotone, nonconstant Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube.
Then some coordinate $i$ has singleton Fourier coefficient at least $\dfrac{9\cdot
9^{-T}}{T^2}$, where $T$ is the total influence of $f$ divided by its variance.
\end{theorem}
